result.text: Title: Ordering in an Online Shop A customer that logs into an E-Shop system and has to wait for its login confirmation (its credentials are checked by the system).
If the login was successful then the customer can continue to select products, else the shopping experience stops.
After selecting a product the customer has to add it to a shopping cart, save the product and check if every product was already selected.
These steps repeat until all products were selected.
Then the order is finished by the shopping system and simultaneously payment and shipment for the order is prepared.
For the payment the customer has to enter its payment data and has to wait until the bank confirms the payment.
While waiting for the payment confirmation the customer can enter its shipping address (an independent billing address can be entered if the shipping address is not equal to the billing address).
Finally if the address and the payment steps are executed then the order will be finished by the system.

Title: Ordering in an Online Shop  

A customer that logs into an E-Shop system and has to wait for its login confirmation (its credentials are checked by the system).
If the login was successful then the customer can continue to select products, else the shopping experience stops.
After selecting a product the customer has to add it to a shopping cart, save the product and check if every product was already selected.
These steps repeat until all products were selected.
Then the order is finished by the shopping system and simultaneously payment and shipment for the order is prepared.
For the payment the customer has to enter its payment data and has to wait until the bank confirms the payment.
While waiting for the payment confirmation the customer can enter its shipping address (an independent billing address can be entered if the shipping address is not equal to the billing address).
Finally if the address and the payment steps are executed then the order will be finished by the system.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Keep each flow node and sequence flow inside its owning process or subprocess. Sequence flows never cross pool or subprocess boundaries.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
Use bpmn:sequenceFlow for execution order between flow nodes in the same process or subprocess scope; set valid sourceRef and targetRef values.

result.rule: When the description states that several activities are all required before a later activity or outcome: Model the activities as parallel branches and synchronize all branches with a parallel gateway before the later activity or outcome.

When the description states that a process begins with a received order, then obtains a choice, and that selected work includes required concurrent activities before a later activity: Connect the start event to the activity that obtains the choice, route the alternatives through a decision gateway, and, where the selected path requires concurrent work, use a parallel split and join before the later activity.

When The description states that one activity is carried out while the result of an already-started activity is still pending.: Model the pending result with an intermediate catch event on one parallel branch and the concurrent activity on another; synchronize the branches before later work that depends on both.

When the description makes completion contingent on both a time-based condition and a separate required activity, without stating that one must precede the other.: Model the time-based wait with an intermediate catch event and the activity as a parallel branch; synchronize the branches with a parallel gateway before completion.

result.rule: Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.

result.rule: When the description says that the process waits for an external participant to confirm or respond: Model receipt of that confirmation or response as an intermediate message catch event, not as a task.

When the description says that a participant is expected to arrive at an unspecified or random time after an activity: Model waiting for that arrival as an intermediate catch event, not as an event-based gateway.

When the description states that a report or message from an external participant conditionally triggers a continuation within an already-running process: Model receipt of the report as an intermediate message catch event in the existing process, rather than as a task or a new start event.
When the description says a participant can enter or provide information before later process actions: Model the information-entry step as an activity, not as a start event.
